brief: Kooth reports H1 2026 revenues of £30.8m with Adjusted EBITDA of £5.0-5.4m, up sharply from £1.6m prior year.
summary: Digital mental health provider Kooth delivered H1 2026 revenues of £30.8m (H1 2025: £32.1m), with planned California product tapering and £0.7m FX headwind offset by Michigan contract gains. Adjusted EBITDA expected £5.0-5.4m versus £1.6m prior year, reflecting strong California user engagement and return to profitability. Net cash position strengthened to £23.1m (H1 2025: £15.3m). California's Soluna platform achieved 187k registrations and external validation via DHCS impact report and Governor's Children and Youth Behavioral Health Initiative.
retail_take: Strong EBITDA recovery and cash generation offset modest revenue decline; California traction and government validation suggest sustainable growth trajectory, likely positive market reception despite revenue headwinds.

headline: Half-year Report
brief: IPF posts H1 pre-exceptional PBT of £47.4m, customer numbers up 5%, receivables up 17%; acquisition by Bidco completing 4 August.
summary: International Personal Finance reported H1-26 pre-exceptional profit before tax of £47.4m (down 5% YoY from £49.9m), reflecting continued investment in growth. Customer numbers increased 5.4% to 1.743m, customer lending grew 18.5%, and closing net receivables rose 17.4% to £1,169.9m. Impairment rate widened to 10.0% from 8.3%, driven by stronger lending growth in new channels. The company maintains £107m headroom on facilities and 48% equity-to-receivables ratio. Recommended acquisition by IPF Parent Holdings (Bidco) expected to complete 4 August 2026 subject to Court sanction on 31 July; special dividend of 15p per share declared, conditional on completion.
retail_take: Solid operational performance with controlled credit quality offset by expected profitability headwinds from IFRS 9 impairments and strategic investment. Acquisition completion imminent reduces forward guidance relevance for independent shareholders; market focus shifts to deal closure and dividend certainty.

headline: Musensi Hill Rare Earth Elements Project, Tanzania
brief: Amigo Resources completes initial geological mapping at Musensi Hill REE project in Tanzania, confirming carbonatite system model.
summary: Amigo's geological team completed systematic mapping and sampling at the Musensi Hill rare earth elements project in Tanzania. Initial XRF screening identified encouraging geochemical indicators including potassium oxide (9-11.7%), calcium oxide (up to 15.1%), strontium (up to 7,000 ppm), and phosphorus pentoxide (up to 7.29%). Results support a multi-phase alkaline-carbonatite interpretation. The company emphasises the screening did not include full REE analysis and cannot determine grade or economic potential. Next phases include complete REE analysis, mineralogy, petrography, and definition of drill targets.
retail_take: Early-stage exploration results are geologically encouraging but commercially non-committal; no mineral resource defined and much work remains before determining economic viability, likely a modest positive for sentiment.

headline: Half Year Trading Update and Notice of Results
Half Yearly Report to 30 June 2026
brief: Imaging Biometrics swings to H1 2026 profitability on 6% revenue growth and 32% cost cuts; IB Clinic gaining clinical traction.
summary: Imaging Biometrics returned to profit in H1 2026 with £73,852 net income versus £89,652 loss prior year. Revenue grew 6% to £416,270; gross profit £414,536. Administrative expenses fell 32% to £325,860, driving operating profit of £88,678. IB Clinic neuro-oncology platform advancing clinical adoption; EAF151 Phase II data presented at ASCO showed superior automated imaging biomarker performance. GaM paediatric cancer programme positioned for partnership; FDA designations in place but development early-stage with 30 September 2029 PRV deadline.
retail_take: Profitable inflection on cost discipline and clinical validation likely reads positively; however, profitability modest and GaM upside heavily caveated and contingent on unproven partnership and regulatory approval by tight deadline.

headline: Molaoi Drilling Update
brief: Molaoi drilling extends high-grade zinc-germanium mineralisation deeper than expected, with grades strengthening at depth.
summary: Hole HMO-019 at Rockfire's 100%-owned Molaoi zinc deposit in Greece returned six mineralised intersections including 0.10m @ 27.8% Zn and 84.1g/t Ge (one of the highest recent germanium values), plus 3.30m @ 18.9% Zn at 261m depth. Results extend mineralisation 50m deeper than previous hole HMO-018, with stronger grades suggesting potential grade increase at depth. Drilling continues upgrading the Inferred Resource to Indicated status; results from HMO-020 awaited. New drilling rig expected September/October; feasibility study advancing with comminution and ore-sorting tests planned.
retail_take: Positive momentum on exploration upside at a critical minerals asset; deeper, higher-grade intersections support near-term resource upgrade path and long-term feasibility study progression, likely supporting sentiment.

summary: Gaming Realms PLC purchased 137,752 ordinary shares on 28 July 2026 at 30.30 pence per share via Peel Hunt LLP on the London Stock Exchange. The shares will be held in treasury. Following this transaction, the company holds 24.7 million treasury shares with 271.5 million shares in issue, representing total voting rights.
retail_take: Routine share buyback execution at consistent pricing; signals capital deployment but provides limited insight into strategic direction or market outlook.

headline: 1st Quarter Results
brief: Maruwa reports Q1 FY2027 results with 11.7% sales growth to ¥19.3bn and 5.8% operating profit rise to ¥6.3bn.
summary: Maruwa Co achieved Q1 FY2027 net sales of ¥19,267m (+11.7% YoY), operating profit ¥6,348m (+5.8%), and net profit ¥4,466m (+15.2%). The Ceramic Components segment grew 10.1% to ¥16,785m; Lighting Equipment surged 23.7% to ¥2,482m on LED demand. Company revised full-year FY2027 forecasts upward to ¥93.3bn sales (+25.3%) and ¥33.7bn operating profit (+34.9%), citing strong telecom and semiconductor demand. Total assets reached ¥165.5bn with equity ratio of 91.5%.
retail_take: Positive earnings beat with significant full-year guidance raise reflects genuine demand acceleration in telecom/semiconductor; capex expansion plans suggest management confidence, though geopolitical headwinds and FX assumptions (158 yen/USD) present execution risks.

headline: June 2026 Quarterly Activities Report
brief: Greatland Resources beat FY26 guidance with 328,987oz gold production; FY27 output expected to decline as investment ramps.
summary: Greatland produced 328,987oz gold at A$2,179/oz AISC in FY26, exceeding 260-310koz guidance. June quarter yielded 79,100oz at A$2,312/oz with 86.8% recovery rates. Cash position strengthened to A$1,289m (debt-free) with A$302m operating cash flow. FY27 guidance: 260-300koz at A$2,900-3,330/oz AISC. Company commencing Havieron pre-production capex (A$365-435m) and Telfer growth investment (A$315-335m), with first Havieron gold expected FY29.
retail_take: Strong operational beat and balance sheet support long-term growth story, but FY27 production decline and elevated AISC guidance signal near-term headwinds from heavy capex and lower ore grades.

brief: LMS Capital NAV falls to 33.0p per share from 35.9p as managed realisation strategy continues with £1.6m capital return.
summary: LMS Capital's NAV declined £2.4m to £26.6m (33.0p per share) at 30 June 2026 from £29.0m (35.9p) at year-end 2025. The decrease reflects a £1.6m capital return in February, £0.2m portfolio losses, offset by £0.2m FX gains from sterling weakness. Cash fell to £2.6m from £6.8m due to capital returns, Dacian loan funding, and Castle View debt repayment. Key holdings: Dacian (energy, £10.8m), Castle View retirement living (£9.4m), and Opus venture fund (£3.0m). Board expects clarity on main asset liquidity by end-2026/early 2027.
retail_take: Modest NAV decline reflects continued capital returns and portfolio challenges; limited near-term catalysts visible, though Board expects strategic clarity within six months, unlikely to move shares meaningfully absent material realisation progress.

headline: 1st Quarter Results
brief: PayPoint reports Q1 FY27 revenue down 6.4% to £39.5m but says it's on track for market expectations with reorganisation embedding successfully.
summary: PayPoint's Q1 FY27 net revenue fell 6.4% to £39.5m from £42.2m, driven by Network Services (down 6.5% to £21.6m) and Love2shop (down 9.8% to £7.0m), offset partly by Digital Payments & Open Banking growth of 4.1% to £3.2m. CEO Nick Wiles highlighted successful business reorganisation embedding with improved retailer engagement, positive momentum in new business wins (Scottish Power, housing clients), and Love2shop's July campaign delivering 103% growth in cards sold. Management expects greater performance weighting to H2 and remains confident in meeting FY27 market expectations; a Capital Markets Day is scheduled for 29 September 2026.
retail_take: Mixed signals: revenue decline against tough comparatives and challenging consumer backdrop offsets by operational improvements and new business traction; market likely cautious until H2 execution demonstrates recovery trajectory.

headline: Transaction in Own Shares
brief: PSH repurchased 32,646 shares at average price of $50.36 on 28 July 2026.
summary: Pershing Square Holdings repurchased 32,646 public shares on 28 July 2026 through agent Jefferies at an average price of $50.36 USD. The buyback comprised 22,370 shares on LSE (PSH ticker) at 3,787 pence average and 10,276 shares (PSHD ticker) at $50.28 average. NAV per share was $76.01 USD as of 21 July. Post-buyback, PSH has 173.55 million shares outstanding with 37.41 million held in treasury.
retail_take: Routine share buyback execution at modest scale; buyback pricing below NAV ($50.36 vs $76.01) suggests potential shareholder value accretion, though announcement provides no strategic context or forward guidance.

headline: NBPE Announces Transaction in Own Shares
brief: NBPE buys back 16,728 Class A shares at £14.48-£14.60; shares to be cancelled.
summary: Neuberger Private Equity Partners Limited repurchased 16,728 Class A shares on 28 July 2026 at prices between £14.48 and £14.60 per share under shareholder authority granted in June 2026. All bought-back shares will be cancelled, reducing outstanding Class A shares to 40,362,573. The company retains 3,150,408 Class A shares in treasury.
retail_take: Routine share buyback execution by closed-end investment company; capital management activity with no material strategic implications for investors.
